anomalies.observed: U3 is labelled ATtiny13V-10S, but its pin assignments are shifted: the drawing shows pin 6 as PB0/SDA, pin 7 as PB1/PWM, and pin 5 as PB2/SCK.
anomalies.expected: For ATtiny13V-10S, and as shown on U2 ATtiny45-20P, pin 5 is PB0, pin 6 is PB1, and pin 7 is PB2; therefore SDA should be on pin 5, PWM on pin 6, and SCK on pin 7.

evidence.quote: U3 ATtiny13V-10S ... 6 PB0 ... 7 PB1 ... 5 PB2 ... SDA/PWM/SCK labels on those pins (sheet /, right tile)
U2 ATtiny45-20P ... 5 AREF/PB0 ... 6 PB1 ... 7 PB2 (sheet /, right tile)

anomalies.impact: If the U3 SMD footprint is populated, the MCU sees/drives SDA, PWM and SCK on the wrong GPIO pins, so firmware written for the ATtiny13/45 pinout will not control the fan or the I2C/SPI interface correctly.

anomalies.observed: The TACH net is pulled up to VCC through R6 10k and also connected to a component D1 valued 1K to GND; D1 is drawn/valued as a 1 kΩ resistor despite the diode reference.
anomalies.expected: A fan tachometer input normally uses only a pull-up or a correctly specified clamp diode; a 1 kΩ resistor to GND would be a strong pulldown, and a diode reference should not carry a resistance value.

evidence.quote: TACH ... D1 1K ... GND and R6 10K TACH VCC (sheet /, top/right area)

anomalies.impact: If D1 is assembled as a 1 kΩ resistor, the TACH input is pulled low by the R6/D1 divider and fan RPM feedback is likely lost; if a diode was intended, the value/reference is wrong.
